reading.body:
CyrusOne's Florence campus is Kentucky's largest published data center at 5 MW of IT capacity, a figure that is small by AI training standards.

Kentucky has three data centers with published power figures, totaling 9.55 MW, so this single campus accounts for more than half the state's disclosed capacity. Five facilities are mapped in the state, and most of them publish no power specification, which makes 9.55 MW a floor rather than a total. The 143,000 square feet of technical space works out to roughly 35 watts per square foot, conventional enterprise density rather than the hundreds of watts per square foot GPU halls require. At 40 kW per rack, 5 MW of IT load is about 125 racks.

The certifications on the campus, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes, describe a facility built for regulated enterprise and government tenants. Those customers buy compliance and uptime, not the power density that AI training needs. By published capacity, Kentucky is not a center of AI scaling activity, and a 5 MW site with this density profile is not a candidate for frontier training workloads without substantial rebuilding of its power and cooling systems.

The record does not say whether CyrusOne intends higher-density retrofits, whether the local grid could serve them, or whether AI tenants are being courted. The suitability score of 50 is a weighted mean of published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing, so it reflects disclosure as much as readiness. No coordinates or nearest airport are resolved in the record, so it supports no claim about proximity to power, fiber, or transport.
